notes: High overlap (6/7 shared claims: C7, C8, C44, C46, C50, C125). Both agree that conditioned media experiments demonstrate suppression by novel bacteria through soluble cues. Peer reviewers explicitly accepted this mechanism without raising concerns.

Shared claims C1, C2, C28, C130 about behavioral phenotype robustness. LLM finds evidence sufficient with adequate statistics and replication. Peer reviewers raised concerns about day-to-day variability (100 pumps/min) being larger than effect size (20 pumps/min) and questioned experimental controls, creating uncertainty about robustness claims.

Shared claims C27, C29, C30, C31 about memory duration and temporal characteristics. LLM finds temporal properties well-established. Peer reviewers' general concerns about day-to-day variability and experimental design cast uncertainty on temporal experiments, which would be particularly sensitive to these methodological issues.

Shared claims C3, C35, C45, C47, C104, C106 about ADF activation and calcium imaging. LLM finds convergent evidence from imaging, rescue, and ablation. Peer reviewers noted incomplete pairwise testing and requested technical details (R values, bleaching rates), indicating calcium imaging data requires additional validation before acceptance.

Shared claims C5, C6, C36, C37, C97, C101, C102 about ADF→serotonin→SER-7(MC)→muscle pathway. Both agree on the circuit mapping through genetic rescue experiments. Peer reviewers asked clarifying questions but did not challenge the mechanism, describing work as 'thorough.'

Shared claims C54, C55, C57, C117, C122 about serotonin release from ADF. Both accept the serotonin release measurements. Peer reviewers did not challenge the indirect uptake assay methodology or ADF's role in releasing serotonin in response to familiar food.

Minimal overlap (C63, C64 about ser-7 mutant phenotypes). LLM finds SER-7's role well-supported through multiple mutant analyses. Peer reviewers' concerns about day-to-day variability and low baseline pumping rates in negative conclusions affect interpretation of mutant phenotypes, creating uncertainty.

Minimal overlap (C61 about serotonin requirement). LLM finds serotonin's role clearly demonstrated through loss- and gain-of-function. Peer reviewers' general methodological concerns about variability and baseline rates indirectly affect confidence in mutant phenotype interpretations.

Minimal overlap (C69, C74 about NSM vs ADF specificity). LLM finds cell-specific rescue experiments clearly distinguish ADF from NSM. Peer reviewers specifically questioned 'negative conclusions from experiments that have control pumping rates on the very low side' affecting NSM non-contribution claims.

Single shared claim C87 about serotonin mediating familiarity response. Both accept serotonin's role in the pathway, though peer review focuses on circuit mapping while LLM emphasizes pharmacological evidence.
Single shared claim C65 about SER-7 receptor role. Both accept SER-7's involvement in the pathway through genetic evidence, though they group this claim with different supporting evidence sets.

Single shared claim C73 about receptor expression/function. LLM finds circuit mapping robust. Peer reviewers' concerns about low baseline rates and variability create uncertainty about negative conclusions in receptor studies.

Claims C66, C67, C82, C134, C135, C136 about inhibitory receptors (SER-4, MOD-1) and triple mutant analysis have no corresponding peer review evaluation. LLM finds this complexity well-documented but no peer assessment available.
